simpler_options.name: Extract Simpler Tree Ancestor Options
simpler_options.summary: Extracts all ancestral prefixes of node X born on earlier days, partitioned into left options (< X) and right options (> X).
simpler_options.domain: X ∈ {+, -}* (Tree Node) ⟹ (XL, XR) where each option has birthday < birthday(X)

complexity.tree: O(d) prefix extractions, where d is the birthday (string depth) of node X
complexity.dyadic: O(1) sign-string prefix slice and set insertion

explanation: Every tree node X is identified by its sign sequence of + and - steps from the root [].
The "options" of X are strictly its ancestral prefixes born on earlier days.
Prefixes smaller than X form the left set XL; prefixes greater form the right set XR.
Guarantees finite inductive reduction by well-founded induction on birthday depth.

cut.name: Conway Cut: Earliest Birthday Node Between Bounds
cut.summary: Finds the unique earliest-born (simplest) Conway tree node strictly between a lower bound and upper bound by binary walking from root [].
cut.domain: leftBound, rightBound ∈ {+, -}* with leftBound < rightBound ⟹ candidate Node

complexity.tree: O(d) tree walk from root [] to the simplest intermediate node born on day d

explanation: The Conway cut embodies the Simplicity Theorem: between any two surreal numbers lies a unique simplest number born on the earliest day.
Begins at the root node [] (0).
If candidate ≤ leftBound, branches right (+) to grow larger.
If candidate ≥ rightBound, branches left (-) to shrink smaller.
Terminates at the unique simplest sign sequence strictly between leftBound and rightBound.

conway_add.name: Conway Inductive Addition
conway_add.summary: Evaluates the exact sum X + Y of two Conway numbers directly on their tree sign paths by recursive options reduction and Conway cut.
conway_add.domain: X, Y ∈ {+, -}* (Tree Nodes, with [] at root 0)

complexity.tree: O(4^d) recursive option calls (explodes exponentially with birthday d)
complexity.dyadic: O(1) aligned bit-shift and 32-bit integer add in the ring (𝔻, +, ·)

explanation: Conway addition recurses over all combinations of simpler ancestors (XL + Y) and (X + YL).
Demonstrates why tree-inductive arithmetic is mathematically fundamental yet computationally explosive.
The Conway cut resolves the final sum as the earliest-born node strictly between maxLeft and minRight.

steps: Recurse ConwayAdd on all 5 left options and 2 right options...

conway_order.name: Conway Inductive Order (X ≤ Y)
conway_order.summary: Determines if node X ≤ Y directly on Conway tree options: no left option of X can be ≥ Y, and no right option of Y can be ≤ X.
conway_order.domain: X, Y ∈ {+, -}* (Tree Nodes) ⟹ 1 if X ≤ Y else 0

complexity.tree: O(2^(d_x + d_y)) mutual recursive option evaluations over earlier birthdays
complexity.dyadic: O(1) sign comparison and bit alignment in the ordered field (𝔻, ≤)

explanation: Conway fundamental inductive definition of order: X ≤ Y ⇔ (∀ xᴸ ∈ Xᴸ, ¬(Y ≤ xᴸ)) ∧ (∀ yᴿ ∈ Yᴿ, ¬(yᴿ ≤ X)).
Base case: 0 ≤ 0 ([] ≤ []) has XL = ∅ and YR = ∅, immediately returning 1 (true).
Inductively generates a total linear order across the entire binary tree without continuous limits or Cauchy sequences.
Grounds the entire field ordering in well-founded induction on birthday depth.

steps: Left loop: XL is empty ⟹ no violation
Right loop: YR is empty ⟹ no violation

conway_sort.name: Conway Total Order Sort
conway_sort.summary: Sorts an array of Conway tree nodes into ascending linear order strictly using the recursive ConwayLessEq order predicate.
conway_sort.domain: A: Array of Node ⟹ Sorted A such that A[0] ≤ A[1] ≤ ... ≤ A[n-1]

complexity.tree: O(n² · 2^d) inductive option comparisons across array elements
complexity.dyadic: O(n log n) standard numeric sort using 64-bit integer compare

explanation: Demonstrates that Conway recursive order defines a true total ordering on any finite collection of surreal numbers.
Uses insertion sort where every pairwise order decision invokes the inductive ConwayLessEq predicate.
Shows how abstract combinatorial game options organize into a strict linear sequence from least to greatest.

steps: Final sorted array satisfies Conway order at every step

conway_sub.name: Conway Inductive Subtraction
conway_sub.summary: Evaluates the exact difference X - Y of two Conway numbers as X + (-Y) via Conway tree negation and addition.

complexity.tree: O(4^d) option tree expansion inherited from ConwayAdd
complexity.dyadic: O(1) aligned bit-shift and integer subtraction in the ring (𝔻, +, ·)

explanation: Conway subtraction reduces directly to addition with the sign-inverted tree node.
Reflects the right-hand argument Y across the root 0 (+ <-> -).
Preserves the group inversion law in the surreal number field.

conway_mul.name: Conway Inductive Multiplication
conway_mul.summary: Evaluates the exact product X · Y of two Conway numbers directly on their tree sign paths via 4-way recursive cross options and Conway cut.

complexity.tree: Hyper-exponential option explosion: each recursive step branches into 4 products, 2 additions, and 1 subtraction
complexity.dyadic: O(1) single integer multiplication and denominator bit addition: (m₁/2^e₁) · (m₂/2^e₂) = (m₁·m₂)/2^(e₁+e₂)

explanation: Conway multiplication is the pinnacle of tree-inductive surreal arithmetic.
Crosses every left and right option pair through 4 distinct algebraic combinations.
Demonstrates why multiplying even small Day 2 numbers triggers dozens of recursive invocations.
The Conway Cut identifies the unique earliest-born surreal product satisfying all option bounds.

conway_neg.name: Conway Tree Negation (-X)
conway_neg.summary: Inverts every sign step (+ <-> -) along the path, reflecting the node across the tree root 0.

complexity.tree: O(d) sign string inversion where d is birthday depth

explanation: Reflects any surreal number across the central root 0.
Positive steps (+) become negative steps (-); negative steps (-) become positive steps (+).
Exact symmetry: ConwayNeg(ConwayNeg(X)) = X.

euler_compounding.name: Euler Hyperfinite Compounding in 𝔻
euler_compounding.summary: Evaluates exp(x) = (1 + x/2^K)^(2^K) using purely dyadic bit-shifts and K repeated squarings in the ring (𝔻, +, ·).
euler_compounding.domain: x ∈ 𝔻 (Dyadic Rational / Tree Node), K ∈ ℕ (e.g. K = 12)

complexity.tree: Zero calculus limits, zero infinite series, zero floating-point math
complexity.dyadic: 1 bit-shift, 1 integer add, K repeated squarings in (𝔻, ·)

explanation: Avoids transcendental library calls and floating-point rounding errors entirely.
Divides unit time into 2^K infinitesimal intervals of width dx = 1/2^K.
Continuous compounding is realized as the exact product of 2^K identical microscopic slices.
Computed in only K iterations via binary repeated squarings in the ring (𝔻, +, ·).

kinematics_step.name: Discrete Kinematic State Update in (𝔻, +, ·)
kinematics_step.summary: Evaluates discrete free-fall velocity v = v₀ ⊖ (g ⊗ t) and trajectory displacement s = (v₀ ⊗ t) ⊖ (1/2 ⊗ g ⊗ t²) strictly in the ring of dyadic rationals.
kinematics_step.domain: v₀, g, t ∈ 𝔻 (Exact Dyadic Rationals on the 2-Successor Tree)

complexity.tree: Finite difference stepping across discrete 2-successor rational tree
complexity.dyadic: Exact integer bit-shifts and ring additions; zero floating-point drift

explanation: Bypasses continuous limits and floating-point math libraries entirely.
Operates purely over the ring of dyadic rationals (𝔻, +, ·) where division by 2 is an exact bit-shift.
Computes both velocity and position synchronously as discrete algebraic difference invariants.
Every state maps directly to a finite Conway tree birthday and unique sign sequence.

example.result: v = 1/2 m/s, s = 20&1/2 m (strictly exact in 𝔻)

cordic_angle.name: Elementary CORDIC Rotation Angle Table
cordic_angle.summary: Provides the exact dyadic elementary rotation angle arctan(2^-i) for iteration step i without transcendental library calls.

complexity.tree: O(1) discrete constant projection from predefined 16-step dyadic lattice
complexity.dyadic: O(1) table lookup with zero runtime transcendentals

explanation: CORDIC rotation relies on an elementary sequence of angles θ_i = arctan(2^-i).
Because tan(θ_i) = 2^-i, multiplying by the tangent reduces to a simple power-of-two bit-shift.
Replaces continuous calculus angles with a finite dyadic table of N discrete steps.

rotor_trig_cordic.name: Dyadic CORDIC Unit Rotor Projection
rotor_trig_cordic.summary: Evaluates circular trigonometric coordinates (cos θ, sin θ) through N discrete dyadic rotations using only power-of-two bit-shifts and additions.
rotor_trig_cordic.domain: θ ∈ 𝔻, step index i ∈ [0 .. N-1] ⟹ coordinate pair (x, y) ∈ 𝔻²

complexity.tree: Discrete angular winding along binary unit circle lattice
complexity.dyadic: N elementary shifts and additions; zero Math.sin / Math.cos dependency

explanation: Eliminates external transcendental math libraries (Math.sin/cos).
At step i, the coordinate vector rotates by angle arctan(2^-i) using only right-shifts (≫ i) and additions (⊕).
Achieves 16-bit precision in only 16 iterations without Taylor series expansions or floating-point division.
Unifies circular geometry with the discrete 2-successor structure of Middle Way arithmetic.

steps: 16 elementary dyadic rotations with elementary angle table...
x converges to 1.0 (node [+]), y converges to 0.0 (node [ ])

laplacian_heat_step.name: Discrete Laplacian Thermal Diffusion in 𝔻
laplacian_heat_step.summary: Advances 1D thermal distribution across spatial slices using the discrete second-difference operator in the ring (𝔻, +, ·).
laplacian_heat_step.domain: T[i] ∈ 𝔻, diffusion coefficient α ∈ 𝔻 (α ≤ 1/2 for stability)

complexity.tree: Local discrete interaction across spatial neighbor tree
complexity.dyadic: O(M) shifts and additions per time-tick; unconditionally exact over 𝔻

explanation: Replaces continuous partial differential equations (PDEs) with exact discrete difference equations in 𝔻.
Multiplying by 2 in the central difference is evaluated as an exact 1-bit left shift (≪ 1).
Guarantees energy conservation and monotonic entropy growth across discrete spatial slices.

bayes_discrete_update.name: Discrete Bayesian Posterior Update in 𝔻
bayes_discrete_update.summary: Computes posterior probability P(H | E) = P(E | H) · P(H) / P(E) over a finite discrete hypothesis partition strictly in (𝔻, +, ·).
bayes_discrete_update.domain: Prior, Likelihood ∈ 𝔻 ∩ [0, 1], Hypothesis Space Ω

complexity.tree: Partition branching on finite hypothesis decision tree
complexity.dyadic: Ring multiplications and dyadic quotient; zero measure-theoretic integrals

explanation: Grounds probability strictly in discrete partition counting over finite event sets.
Joint likelihoods are exact dyadic products in the ring (𝔻, +, ·).
Normalizing evidence P(E) is evaluated as the exact sum of disjoint joint weights.
Produces a verifiable rational probability without real-analysis measure theory.

maximum.name: Option Set Supremum (Maximum)
maximum.summary: Scans a finite set of Conway tree options to find the maximal (greatest) node according to the surreal tree order.
maximum.domain: S ⊂ {+, -}* (Finite Option Set) ⟹ m ∈ S such that ∀ x ∈ S, x ≤ m

complexity.tree: O(|S|) comparisons along binary sign trees

explanation: Finds the supremum over a finite set of surreal tree options.
Initializes candidate maximum to nil (unassigned empty bound).
Iterates over each candidate option x in set S.
Updates maximum m whenever an option is strictly greater (x > m) under Conway tree order.
Essential for Conway addition and inductive game options resolution.

minimum.name: Option Set Infimum (Minimum)
minimum.summary: Scans a finite set of Conway tree options to find the minimal (least) node according to the surreal tree order.
minimum.domain: S ⊂ {+, -}* (Finite Option Set) ⟹ m ∈ S such that ∀ x ∈ S, x ≥ m

complexity.tree: O(|S|) comparisons along binary sign trees

explanation: Finds the infimum over a finite set of surreal tree options.
Initializes candidate minimum to nil (unassigned empty bound).
Iterates over each candidate option x in set S.
Updates minimum m whenever an option is strictly smaller (x < m) under Conway tree order.
Forms the right bound in the Conway cut resolution.

empty_set.name: Empty Option Set Allocator
empty_set.summary: Initializes an empty finite discrete option collection ∅ born before the current generation day.

complexity.tree: O(1) allocation of empty ancestor collection

explanation: All surreal inductive definitions ground in the empty option set ∅.
The surreal number zero is defined by 0 = { ∅ | ∅ } on Day 0.
Initializes clean accumulator sets for left options (XL) and right options (XR).

insert.name: Option Set Inclusion
insert.summary: Inserts candidate tree node into an ancestral option collection S if not already present.

complexity.tree: O(|S|) prefix equality checks

explanation: Maintains set uniqueness when aggregating cross-recursive option sums.
Checks whether the tree node item is already present in S.
Inserts the element into S if unique, ensuring option sets remain strictly finite and deduplicated.

length.name: Birthday Depth (length)
length.summary: Returns the string length (birthday depth) of node X from the root [].

complexity.tree: O(1) step count query on path string

explanation: The length of a sign sequence is its birthday: the generation day d on which number X was created.
Root [] has length 0 (Day 0).
Numbers [+], [-] have length 1 (Day 1).
Limits ancestor prefix loops to strictly earlier generations: 0 to length(X) - 1.

sqr.name: Exact Dyadic Squaring
sqr.summary: Evaluates the exact square u² of a dyadic rational via a single multiplication in the ring (𝔻, ·).

complexity.tree: Finite convolution of sign path numerators

explanation: Computes u² strictly within the ring of dyadic rationals.
If u = m / 2^e, then u² = m² / 2^(2e), staying strictly inside 𝔻.
Core foundation of Euler hyperfinite compounding: enables (1 + x/2^K)^(2^K) in only K squarings.

val.name: Rational Projection (val)
val.summary: Extracts the exact rational value d ∈ 𝔻 from a Conway tree node sign sequence.

complexity.tree: O(d) binary Horner evaluation of sign string

explanation: Bridges the tree-inductive realm and the algebraic ring (𝔻, +, ·).
Interprets the sign path as an integer part followed by binary fractional bits.
Allows algorithms to switch into fast machine arithmetic when continuous or transcendental rates are required.

steps: Root 0 ➔ branch right (+) to 1 ➔ branch left (-) to 1/2

node.name: Canonical Tree Projection (node)
node.summary: Maps a dyadic rational d ∈ 𝔻 to its unique earliest sign path on the binary tree.
node.domain: d ∈ 𝔻 ⟹ unique simplest node X ∈ {+, -}*

complexity.tree: O(e) tree descent to earliest born rational

explanation: The inverse of val: projects an algebraic dyadic rational back into the geometric Conway tree.
Guaranteed to produce the canonical, shortest sign string representing d.
Enables results from Euler compounding, kinematics, or CORDIC to be displayed directly on the visual tree.

create_array.name: Lattice Array Allocation
create_array.summary: Allocates a spatial 1D grid array of M discrete dyadic cells initialized to root [].
create_array.domain: M ∈ ℕ ⟹ Array[0 .. M-1] of Dyadic

complexity.tree: O(M) tree root references

explanation: Initializes discrete spatial domain for 1D diffusion and wave PDE stepping.
Allocates M discrete cells, each initialized to 0 (root []).
Provides indexed boundary access nextT[0] and interior iteration nextT[i].

cordic_angle_table.name: Elementary CORDIC Angle Table
cordic_angle_table.summary: Provides the exact elementary rotation angle arctan(2^-i) for step i.

complexity.tree: O(1) constant projection

explanation: Provides the predefined constants arctan(2^-i) where tangent is exactly 2^-i.
Multiplication by the tangent reduces to a simple power-of-two right bit-shift (≫ i).
Stores 16 elementary angles, providing 16-bit trigonometric accuracy with zero runtime transcendental overhead.

op_add.name: Dyadic Ring Addition (⊕)
op_add.summary: Evaluates exact dyadic addition with power-of-two denominator alignment in the ring (𝔻, +, ·).
op_add.domain: a, b ∈ 𝔻 ⟹ a ⊕ b ∈ 𝔻

complexity.tree: Replaces Conway inductive recursion O(4^d) with exact O(1) ring addition

explanation: The foundational operation of the dyadic machine.
Aligns denominators via bit-shifts and sums 64-bit integer numerators.
Never introduces floating-point rounding error; mathematically exact.

steps: Shift b to common denominator 4: b = 2/4

op_concat.name: Tree Branch Concatenation (++)
op_concat.summary: Appends a discrete sign step (+ for right branch, - for left branch) to walk down the binary tree.

complexity.tree: 1 step down the binary Conway tree

explanation: Navigates down the Conway surreal tree one generation step at a time.
Appending + moves to a larger child (right branch).
Appending - moves to a smaller child (left branch).
Used by the Conway Cut to walk from the root [] to the simplest intermediate node.
